 (By Sri. K.Chandra Shekar.,Adv.,)
 Judgment

The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 19.11.2021.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 19.11.2021 at about 7.30 to 7.45 p.m. the petitioner after attending the Sathyanarayana pooja with his friend was returning back from Doddaballapura to his home at Bengaluru by riding a motor cycle bearing No. KA-05-KW-0218 on the extreme left side of Vidyapeeta circle U Turn, Singanayakanahalli village, Yelahanka Hobli, Doddballapura main road, at that time the driver of Tata Ace bearing No.
KA-04-AC-2346 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Navachetana Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and he has spent Rs.8,30,000/- towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as Cash Operation New Associate at Accenture Solution Pvt. Ltd., and earning Rs.35,029/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices, both the respondents appeared.
The respondent No.2 has filed written statement and the respondent No.1 has not chosen to file any written statement.
Respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by denying the issuance of policy to the Tata Ace bearing No. KA-04-AC-2346.
Further contended that, the accident was happened due to negligence on the part of the petitioner himself as he was riding the motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner.
Also contended that the driver of the Tata Ace was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Further denied the age, avocation, alleged disability and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
Shivu.
N vs Syed Babji

on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185247445/
2

1. Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Tata Ace bearing No.KA-04-AC-2346 by its driver, in RTA took place on 19.11.2021 at about 7.30 p.m. on Vishwa Vidyapeeta circle U turn near Singanayakanahalli village, Yelahanka Hobli, Yelahanka Taluk, Bengaluru?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, at what amount and from whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 14.
Dr. Nagaraj B.N., who is working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Centre, is examined as PW.2, through him got marked Ex.P15 & 16.
In spite of sufficient opportunities, the respondents did not chose to adduce evidence.

6. I have heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar along with sketch, IMV report and charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 5.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR which is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by the father of the petitioner.
In the contents of Ex.P.1 & 2 is in consonance with the petition averments.
After the registration of FIR as per Ex.P1, the Ex.P4 spot mahazar was conducted.
On perusal of the contents of Ex.P4 spot mahazar therein, the alleged accident place is near the U turn.
The photographs which is available in the Ex.P4 also shows the place of accident.

Thus, the contents of Ex.P4 mahazar supported the case of the petitioner regarding the rash and negligence driving by the driver of the Tata Ace KA-04-AC-2346.
10.

The Ex.P7 is IMV report of the both the vehicles wherein the Tata Ace KA-04-AC-2346 has got damaged in its left side and the bike in which the petitioner was proceeding has got damaged in its right and front side which also once again supported the case of the petitioner regarding the rash Shivu.N vs Syed Babji on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185247445/
3 and negligent driving by the driver of the Tata Ace KA-04-AC-2346.
As discussed above, as per mahazar the accident is near the U turn wherein the driver of Tata Ace KA-04-AC-2346 came from opposite side and dashed against the bike of the petitioner.
Thus the Ex.P7 once again successfully established the negligence on the part of driver of Tata Ace KA-04-AC-2346.
Ex.P3 charge sheet is also came to be filed on the driver of the offending Tata Ace KA-04-AC- 2346.
wherein, the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of driver of Tata Ace KA-04-AC-2346.
It is very important to note that the respondent No.1 being the owner and driver of Tata Ace KA-04-AC-2346 made as accused No.1 in the said criminal case.

11. In the present petition filed by seeking compensation, the respondent No.1 who is the owner and driver of Tata Ace KA-04-AC-2346 appeared through his counsel but does not chosen to file written statement or to lead rebuttal evidence to deny the case of the petitioner.
No grounds are made out by the respondents to show that contributory negligence from the petitioner.
12. The respondent No.2- insurance company has filed written statement by denying the negligence and their liability.
But both the respondents have not lead any evidence to rebut the case of the petitioner.
As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the driver of offending vehicle.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Tata Ace KA-04-AC-2346.
13.
The first respondent who is the owner and driver of the offending vehicle does not chosen to deny the allegation of the rash and negligence driving.
The respondent no.2 even though filed written statement, has failed to establish the negligence on the part of the petitioner for the occurrence of the accident.
The respondent No.1 & 2 even after sufficient opportunity have not lead any evidence to disprove the contents of these documents.

The charge sheet is came to be filed against the respondent No.1 who is the driver and owner of the the offending vehicle Tata Ace KA-04-AC-2346 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 of IPC along with Sec 187 of IMV Act.

2009 ACJ 287 ( National Ins. Co. V/s.
Pushparama and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

14. Hence, by relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents marked at Ex.P1 to 9, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the Tata Ace KA-04-AC-2346.

15. In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond Shivu.N vs Syed Babji on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185247445/
4
reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

entities.text: 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

16. In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent no.2 made a suggestions to the petitioner by stating that the accident was occurred by his negligence, nothing being elicited or produced to probabalise the said defence.
17. The contents of Ex.P4 spot mahazar and Ex.P7- IMV report falsifies the contention of respondent no.2 about the contributory negligence by the petitioner for the occurrence of accident.

In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 9 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.

The Ex.P3 charge sheet also supports the view of this court, as the charge sheet filed for the offence punishable under Sec. 279, 337 & 338 of IPC and 187 of IMV Act against the driver of the Tata Ace KA-04-AC-2346.
18.
As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 19.11.2021 which is caused by the driver of the Tata Ace KA-04-AC-2346. which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
19.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY :- At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 24 years.
The petitioner has not produced Aadhaar card.
But in the discharge summary produced at Ex.P10 shows that the petitioner was aged about 24 years at the time of accident.

As per the discharge summary the petitioner was admitted to Navachetana Hospital on 19.11.2021 and discharged on 24.11.2021 and he has sustained comminuted fracture shaft of right femur and displaced fracture of right ulna.
He underwent interlock nailing for right femur and ORIF with plate and screws Shivu.
N vs Syed Babji
on 17 January, 2024

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185247445/
5 for right ulna fracture.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.25,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.

b) Medical expenses: The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P11 & 13,
amounting to Rs.1,57,299/-.

At the time of cross-examination the Pw.1/ petitioner has admitted that, out of the medical expenditure he has received 70%
reimbursement and 30% is paid by him.
But no documents is produced by the petitioner to show the exact amount paid by the health insurance.
The bill dated 19.11.2021 of Navachetana Hospital which is marked at Ex.P11 is the inpatient bill.
The said bill does not bear the seal and signature of the hospital.
Usually the inpatient bills will be reimbursed by the health insurance company.

Hence, in the absence of specific documents in this regard, this court is of the opinion that the inpatient bill produced by the petitioner cannot be considered under this head as the petitioner admitted about the reimbursement.
Hence, the amount of remaining bills can be granted under this head i.e., Rs.22,997/-, the said amount is rounded off to Rs.23,000/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was working as cash operation New Associate at Accenture Solution Pvt. Ltd., and earning Rs.35,029/- p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has produced bank statement as per Ex.P.14.
As per the discharge summary marked at ExP10 the petitioner was admitted to Navachetana Hospital for 6 days from 19.11.2021 to 24.11.2021.
By considering the said aspect, this court is of the opinion that the petitioner might have taken the time of twenty days for his recovery.
Hence, the said period has to be taken under the head of loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,200/- during the laid up period d)
Disability:-
In the cross-examination the petitioner admitted that he is continued with the earlier job.
Hence, in lieu of the said admission this tribunal can infer that there is no disability caused to the petitioner and he is not entitle for the compensation under this head.

In this regard, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 relied on the following judgment wherein it is held as follows;
Sri. Subash V/s. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Represented its Manager and Others reported in ILR 2010 KAR 2439 wherein it is held that;-

entities.text: Sri. Subash V/s. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As rightly pointed out by Learned Counsel appearing for insurer, the Tribunal has grossly erred in awarding compensation towards loss of future income, resulting in serious miscarriage of justice,
when in fact, t he claimant has been continued in the services of the Corporation as ' Conductor'.
If the claimant is continued in serive, then the question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise.

Shivu.N vs Syed Babji on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185247445/
6

Therefore, taking this aspect into consideration, without going into further merits and demerits of the case, we hereby set aside the compensation of Rs.1,86,525/-
awarded by Tribunal towards loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE ; As per Ex.P10 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 6 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P7 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are simple and grievous in nature.

By considering the nature of the injuries and the period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 6 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the injuries as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.6,000/- in total.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.10,000/- under this head.
h)Towards future medical expenses: PW.2 stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants, which may costs Rs.60,000/-.
But he has not produced any estimation or relevant documents to show the need of further treatments.
The evidence of PW.2- doctor even though stated about the surgery for removal of implant, no estimation is produced.

At the time of cross-examination nothing been elicited to hold that the implants are already removed hence, by considering the same Rs.15,000/- may be granted for future medical expenses i.e., for the removal of implants.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a) Towards pain and agony Rs. 25,000/-
b) Towards medical expenses Rs. 23,000/-
c) Towards loss of income Rs. 20,200/-
d) Towards disability NIL e) Towards food, nourishment Shivu.N vs Syed Babji on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185247445/
7  and conveyance Rs. 10,000/-
f) Towards attendant charges Rs. 6,000/-
g) Towards loss of amenities Rs. 10,000/-

h) Towards future medical  expenses Rs. 15,000/-
 _______________
. Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has denied the issuance of policy to the tata ace bearing No. KA-04-AC-2346.
On perusal of the contents of Ex.P6 reply given by the owner of offending vehicle was having valid licence at the time of alleged accident.
The policy number is mentioned at Ex.P6- IMV reply.
On considering the Ex.P3 charge sheet no offences are invoked against the owner of the offending vehicle for not having valid licence.
The respondent No.2 insurance company even though has denied the issuance of insurance policy has not examined or adduced any evidence in support of their contention.

21. The trial of claim petitions is based on preponderance of probabilities wherein in the absence of rebuttal evidence, the respondent has failed to prove that the offending vehicle was not having valid licence cannot be accepted.

Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
22.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
O RDE R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.1,09,200/- (Rupees One lakh nine thousand two hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
Shivu.N vs Syed Babji on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185247445/
8
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the amount awarded, it is ordered to release the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
